T=[\begin{aligned}0 & 7 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

If $\,T\,$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $\,T,$ find $\,T(v).$

examples.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $\mathbf{v}$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ find $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14048912/assets/8ddf6015972344b2afaccf34a63e5ae8c478f326a2b227c45499a1be168ce996.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v})=T\cdot \mathbf{v},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ -6 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}27 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
What is the linear transformation $T$ whose standard matrix is $T=[\begin{aligned}8 & -2 & -3 \\ -4 & 9 & 6 \\ 5 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}]?$

| $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
|  | {{field-3}} |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
Consider a general vector $\,[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}].$ Multiplying by the matrix $T,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -2 & -3 \\ -4 & 9 & 6 \\ 5 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8x-2y-3z \\ -4x+9y+6z \\ 5x-7y+2z\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\,T\,$ is given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}8x-2y-3z \\ -4x+9y+6z \\ 5x-7y+2z\end{aligned}].
$$
